1. Open the starwars dataset (located in tidyverse)
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
data("starwars")
```

2. Create a scatter plot of character's height and mass.
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, mass))+ geom_point()
```

2a. Change the color and shape of the points in your scatter plot. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, mass))+ geom_point(shape= 5, color="purple")
```

3. Add Homeworld as a third variable to your scatterplot. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, mass, color=homeworld))+ geom_point()
```

3a. What do you notice about the graph? (e.g. describe what you see)
**There is a lot of rows for Homeworld, each are in a different color (rainbow), and each dot (character) is colored by their Homeworld. Also, most of the data is at the bottom of the plot but there is an outlier with a mass over 1000 which makes it difficult to look at each data point individually.**

4. Make a boxplot of height. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(y= height))+ geom_boxplot()
```

5. Make a boxplot of height for each species present in the data.
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(x= species, y= height))+ geom_boxplot()
```

5a. change the appearance of your graph in at least 3 ways.
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(species, height))+ geom_boxplot(fill= "white", color="purple")+ theme_classic()+ ggtitle(label = "Height of species")

#1. added color
#2. added theme
#3. added label
```

6. Using any variables in the starwars dataset, create a graph that uses a color palette from viridis.
```{r}
library(viridis)
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, mass, color=gender))+ geom_point()+ scale_fill_viridis(option="plasma", discrete=TRUE)
```

7.Using any variables in the starwars dataset, create a graph that uses a color palette from RColorBrewer.
```{r}
library(RColorBrewer)
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, mass, color=gender))+ geom_point()+ scale_color_brewer(palette="Blues") 
```

8. Using any variables in the starwars dataset, create a graph using facet_wrap
```{r}
heightMassColor<- ggplot(starwars, aes(height, mass, color= gender))+ geom_boxplot()+ facet_wrap(~gender)
```
